model_interpretation.claim: The previous valid OpenMP candidate used a serial cutoff of 512 options per requested worker. Lowering the cutoff to 256 options per effective worker, while limiting the requested team to min(threads, n), tests whether parallelizing medium workloads pays off without creating idle workers or exceeding the passed CPU budget. The controller must measure the cutoff's overhead and any gain; no result is assumed here.

model_interpretation.claim: The independent option calculations can be distributed with a static OpenMP outer loop, while num_threads(threads) caps the requested team at the passed budget. A serial path for one thread and fewer than 512 options per requested thread should avoid paying parallel-region overhead on small workloads. Each loop iteration writes exactly its own result index; the controller still needs to verify correctness and measure the tradeoff.

model_interpretation.claim: The prior OpenMP candidate was valid on eight varied correctness cases and measured 1.430 ms mean versus the serial baseline's 7.529 ms mean under this campaign. That observation alone does not isolate the cause of the difference or establish a cutoff optimum.
model_interpretation.applicability: Useful evidence that the outer loop can be parallelized while preserving varied-input correctness; it does not identify an optimal small-work cutoff or establish speedup for this candidate.
model_interpretation.next_experiment: Measure this lower per-worker cutoff, especially cases near the serial/parallel boundary and available thread counts, and compare overhead with the prior candidate.

items.subject: OpenMP scaling and overhead within the threads budget
items.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare the serial baseline with an OpenMP outer loop using the passed threads value as a hard CPU budget; start with static scheduling and retain a serial path for one thread or small n. Avoid thresholds tied to published test values. Measure available valid n/thread cases under the frozen protocol, verify complete output writes and varied-input correctness, and report overhead as well as any gain. Preserve correct variants for later combination even if they lose in isolation.
